docs.text:
tyro_flags_toop.help_text runs python -m toop_engine_topology_optimizer.dc.main --help (244 lines; it needs PYTHONUTF8=1 on a Windows console) and flag_table checks eight flags against the Pydantic fields:

Flag Field Default --fixed-files CLIArgs.fixed_files () --double-limits CLIArgs.double_limits (1.0, 1.0) --ga-config.runtime-seconds BatchedMEParameters.runtime_seconds 60 --ga-config.random-seed BatchedMEParameters.random_seed 42 --ga-config.n-worst-contingencies BatchedMEParameters.n_worst_contingencies 20 --ga-config.me-descriptors.0.num-cells DescriptorDef.num_cells (first descriptor) required --lf-config.max-num-splits LoadflowSolverParameters.max_num_splits 4 --lf-config.batch-size LoadflowSolverParameters.batch_size 8

tyro reads the type annotations of CLIArgs: a field whose type is itself a Pydantic model (ga_config: BatchedMEParameters, lf_config: LoadflowSolverParameters) becomes a group of flags named --<field>.<subfield> with underscores turned into dashes, printed as its own box ("ga-config options") whose header is the field's docstring; nested further, the first element of the default me_descriptors tuple becomes the group ga-config.me-descriptors.0. Booleans become a pair, --ga-config.enable-nodal-inj-optim and --ga-config.no-enable-nodal-inj-optim; tuples take several values (--double-limits FLOAT FLOAT); Literal and enum types are rendered as a choice set (the long {max_flow_n_0,median_flow_n_0,...} of target-metrics); each flag's help text is the attribute docstring of the field, and its default is the Pydantic default. The parsed values are fed back through CLIArgs(**...), so Pydantic's validators still run after tyro.

tyro_flags_toop.py
"""The tyro command line of ToOp's DC optimizer and the Pydantic fields behind its flags (Chapter 34, Exercise 4).

Run with ToOp's interpreter from this folder::

    ../../../../../ToOp/.venv/Scripts/python.exe tyro_flags_toop.py

``python -m toop_engine_topology_optimizer.dc.main --help`` is run in a subprocess with ``PYTHONUTF8=1``: tyro
draws its help with box characters, which crash on a cp1252 Windows console (``UnicodeEncodeError`` in colorama).
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys

from toop_engine_topology_optimizer.dc.main import CLIArgs
from toop_engine_topology_optimizer.interfaces.messages.commons import DescriptorDef
from toop_engine_topology_optimizer.interfaces.messages.dc_params import BatchedMEParameters, LoadflowSolverParameters

# flag -> (model, field): tyro turns a nested Pydantic model into dotted flags, snake_case becoming kebab-case
FLAGS = {
    '--fixed-files': (CLIArgs, 'fixed_files'),
    '--double-limits': (CLIArgs, 'double_limits'),
    '--ga-config.runtime-seconds': (BatchedMEParameters, 'runtime_seconds'),
    '--ga-config.random-seed': (BatchedMEParameters, 'random_seed'),
    '--ga-config.n-worst-contingencies': (BatchedMEParameters, 'n_worst_contingencies'),
    '--ga-config.me-descriptors.0.num-cells': (DescriptorDef, 'num_cells'),
    '--lf-config.max-num-splits': (LoadflowSolverParameters, 'max_num_splits'),
    '--lf-config.batch-size': (LoadflowSolverParameters, 'batch_size'),
}


def help_text():
    """The ``--help`` output of the DC optimizer CLI."""
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUTF8='1')
    result = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603
        [sys.executable, '-m', 'toop_engine_topology_optimizer.dc.main', '--help'],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding='utf-8',
        env=env,
        check=True,
    )
    return result.stdout


def flag_table(text):
    """For every flag of ``FLAGS``: present in the help, and the field's declared default."""
    rows = {}
    for flag, (model, field) in FLAGS.items():
        info = model.model_fields[field]
        rows[flag] = {
            'present': flag in text,
            'model': model.__name__,
            'field': field,
            'default': info.get_default(call_default_factory=True),
        }
    return rows


def main():
    """Print the mapping and the boolean-flag convention."""
    text = help_text()
    print(f'help text: {len(text.splitlines())} lines')
    for flag, row in flag_table(text).items():
        status = 'ok ' if row['present'] else 'MISSING'
        print(f'  {flag:42s} {status} {row["model"]}.{row["field"]} (default {row["default"]!r})')
    booleans = [
        line.strip(' \u2502') for line in text.splitlines() if '--ga-config.no-' in line or '--lf-config.no-' in line
    ]
    print('boolean fields become a pair of flags, for example:', booleans[:2])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: Exercise 5
docs.text:
Run in the course image toop-course:cpu (built from the course fork's docker/Dockerfile) with ToOp commit ba1874e bind-mounted read-only at /app; Docker Desktop's VM had 16 CPUs and 13.6 GB, shared with other ToOp containers. From Git Bash, in the ToOp checkout, once with --shm-size=64m (Docker's default, written out) and once with --shm-size=2gb:

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker run --rm --shm-size=64m -v "$(pwd -W):/app:ro" -w /app toop-course:cpu \
  bash -c 'df -h /dev/shm; uv run pytest packages/contingency_analysis_pkg/tests/pandapower/test_contingency_analysis_pandapower.py -q --junit-xml=/tmp/r.xml'

(--junit-xml=/tmp/... only keeps ToOp's addopts from writing test-report.xml into the read-only /app.)

--shm-size df -h /dev/shm Result pytest time 64m 64M 14 passed, 1 skipped, 1010 warnings 158.89 s 2gb 2.0G 14 passed, 1 skipped, 1010 warnings 146.09 s

The outcome is the same: no failure and no message about shared memory in either run. The skipped test is test_run_ac_contingency_analysis_pandapower_mt, marked skip(reason="Does not work on CI"); the others that take the init_ray fixture start a local Ray 2.57.0 instance. The time difference is within the noise of a shared machine. Two small programs in the chapter's src folder show why, run in the same container from the course checkout (mounted at /course) with python shm_fill.py 200 and python ray_store_toop.py (the store size and the timing move by a few MB and hundredths of a second from run to run):

--shm-size shm_fill.py 200 Ray object store Store moved out of /dev/shm ray.put of 200 MB 64m return code −7 (SIGBUS) 4073 MB yes 0.46 s 2gb return code 0 4077 MB yes 0.36 s 4.5gb return code 0 4076 MB no 0.28 s
  • Ray does not need /dev/shm. It sizes its object store at 30 % of the memory it sees (4 GB of the VM's 13.6 GB) and, when /dev/shm is smaller, logs WARNING: The object store is using /tmp/ray instead of /dev/shm because /dev/shm has only 67108864 bytes available. This will harm performance!, suggesting --shm-size=4.38gb, and carries on with a disk-backed store. With 2 GB the warning is the same (2147483648 bytes); only from 4.5 GB does the store stay in /dev/shm. pytest captures the log of passing tests, so in the runs above the warning was never shown. With --shm-size=2gb, as the compose file sets, Ray still runs on the fallback.
  • A write past the end of /dev/shm is a signal, not an error. shm_fill.py creates a 200 MB multiprocessing.shared_memory segment, which always succeeds because tmpfs only records the length, then writes every byte in a child process. With 64 MB the kernel has no page to back the 65th megabyte and kills the writer with SIGBUS: the child's return code is −7, and the shell reports Bus error (core dumped) and exit status 135 (128 + 7). There is no Python exception, no ENOSPC, and nothing that names shared memory: the process that ran out of /dev/shm is dead before it can say so, and whatever supervises it (Ray, a ProcessPoolExecutor) reports a worker that died. With 2 GB the same fill succeeds.

So a small /dev/shm shows up either as a performance warning nobody reads or as a crashed process with no explanation, never as "out of shared memory", because the limit is a mount size and the failing operation is an ordinary memory write. The chapter's advice still holds: pass --shm-size (or the compose file's shm_size) large enough for the heaviest user, and when a worker dies in a container, check /dev/shm and exit code 137 first. When the driver is started with uv run, Ray also packages the working directory for its workers (12.87 MiB of /app, about 30 s before the first task here); ray_store_toop.py sets RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0, as ToOp's CI does, to skip that.

shm_fill.py
"""Fill a shared-memory segment larger than /dev/shm and see how the process dies (Chapter 34, Exercise 5).

Run it inside the ToOp container, once per ``--shm-size``, with the size of the segment in MB::

    python shm_fill.py 200

Creating the segment always succeeds: ``ftruncate`` on tmpfs only records a length and reserves nothing. The
pages are allocated when they are first written, and when ``/dev/shm`` has none left the kernel cannot back the
page and sends ``SIGBUS`` to the writer. There is no exception and no "out of shared memory" message: the
process is simply killed, so the fill runs in a child process and this script reports how the child ended.
Standard library only; it runs anywhere ``multiprocessing.shared_memory`` exists (on Windows the segment is a
named file mapping and the fill succeeds).
"""

import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
from multiprocessing import shared_memory
from pathlib import Path

SHM = Path('/dev/shm')  # noqa: S108 -- the shared-memory mount being measured, not a temporary file


def shm_bytes():
    """Size of the ``/dev/shm`` file system in bytes, or ``None`` where there is none (Windows, macOS)."""
    return shutil.disk_usage(SHM).total if SHM.is_dir() else None


def fill(mb):
    """Create a segment of ``mb`` MB, write a byte into every position, then release it."""
    segment = shared_memory.SharedMemory(create=True, size=mb * 2**20)
    try:
        segment.buf[:] = b'\x01' * segment.size
    finally:
        segment.close()
        segment.unlink()


def fill_in_child(mb):
    """Run :func:`fill` in a child interpreter and return its return code (negative: killed by that signal)."""
    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__, '--child', str(mb)], capture_output=True, check=False)  # noqa: S603
    return result.returncode


def describe(returncode):
    """``exit 0``, ``exit 1`` or the name of the signal that killed the child (``SIGBUS``)."""
    if returncode >= 0:
        return f'exit {returncode}'
    try:
        return signal.Signals(-returncode).name
    except ValueError:
        return f'signal {-returncode}'


def main():
    """Print the numbers quoted in the solution of Exercise 5."""
    if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == '--child':
        fill(int(sys.argv[2]))
        return
    mb = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 200
    size = shm_bytes()
    print(f'{SHM} size MB:', 'none' if size is None else round(size / 2**20))
    returncode = fill_in_child(mb)
    print(f'fill of {mb} MB: return code {returncode} ({describe(returncode)})')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

ray_store_toop.py
"""Where Ray puts its object store, and what it says about /dev/shm (Chapter 34, Exercise 5).

Run it inside the ToOp container, once per ``--shm-size``::

    python ray_store_toop.py

Ray sizes its object store at 30 % of the memory it sees and, when ``/dev/shm`` is smaller than that, logs a
warning and puts the store in its temporary folder instead (disk-backed, slower). Nothing fails, which is why a
small ``/dev/shm`` does not show up as an error in a test run: pytest captures the warning with the rest of the
log. ``RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0`` (as in ToOp's CI) stops Ray from packaging the working directory for
its workers when the driver was started by ``uv run``.
"""

import logging
import os
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

os.environ.setdefault('RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV', '0')

import ray  # noqa: E402

SHM = Path('/dev/shm')  # noqa: S108 -- the shared-memory mount being measured, not a temporary file


class _Collect(logging.Handler):
    """Keep the messages of Ray's log records."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(logging.WARNING)
        self.messages = []

    def emit(self, record):
        self.messages.append(record.getMessage())


def object_store(put_mb=200):
    """Start a local Ray instance, put ``put_mb`` MB into its object store, read it back and shut down.

    Returns the ``/dev/shm`` size (``None`` where there is none), the object-store size Ray chose, whether Ray
    warned that the store left ``/dev/shm``, the time of the ``put`` and whether the data came back intact.
    """
    collect = _Collect()
    ray_logger = logging.getLogger('ray')
    ray_logger.addHandler(collect)
    try:
        ray.init(include_dashboard=False, ignore_reinit_error=True, log_to_driver=False)
        store_bytes = ray.available_resources()['object_store_memory']
        data = np.ones(put_mb * 2**20 // 8)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        ref = ray.put(data)
        put_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        intact = float(ray.get(ref).sum()) == data.size
    finally:
        ray.shutdown()
        ray_logger.removeHandler(collect)
    return {
        'shm_mb': round(shutil.disk_usage(SHM).total / 2**20) if SHM.is_dir() else None,
        'object_store_mb': round(store_bytes / 2**20),
        'fallback_warning': next((m for m in collect.messages if 'instead of /dev/shm' in m), None),
        'put_seconds': put_seconds,
        'intact': intact,
    }


def main():
    """Print the numbers quoted in the solution of Exercise 5."""
    result = object_store()
    print('ray', ray.__version__)
    print(f'{SHM} size MB:', result['shm_mb'])
    print('object store MB:', result['object_store_mb'])
    print(f'store moved out of {SHM}:', result['fallback_warning'] is not None)
    if result['fallback_warning']:
        print('  ' + result['fallback_warning'].split(' This will')[0])
    print(f'put 200 MB: {result["put_seconds"]:.2f} s, read back intact: {result["intact"]}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Open the src/ folder on GitHub to see or download all the files of this chapter.

docs.title: Exercise 6
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph gpu["GPU node"]
        DC["DC worker<br/>optimizer/dc/worker/worker.py<br/>state: JAX repertoire in device memory"]
    end
    subgraph cpu1["CPU node 1"]
        AC1["AC worker 1<br/>optimizer/ac/worker.py<br/>state: in-memory SQLite (ACOptimTopology)"]
    end
    subgraph cpu2["CPU node 2"]
        AC2["AC worker 2<br/>in-memory SQLite"]
    end
    subgraph cpu3["CPU node 3"]
        AC3["AC worker 3<br/>in-memory SQLite"]
    end
    subgraph kafka["Kafka (durable log, replayable)"]
        CMD[("commands")]
        RES[("results")]
        HB[("heartbeat")]
        ICMD[("importer_commands / importer_results / importer_heartbeat")]
    end
    subgraph fs["Shared file system (durable)"]
        GRID["processed grid folder<br/>static_information.hdf5, action_set.*, grid.xiidm, masks/"]
        LF["load-flow results folder<br/>loadflow_result_fs"]
    end
    IMP["Importer / preprocessing worker"] --> GRID
    IMP --> ICMD
    CMD --> DC
    CMD --> AC1
    CMD --> AC2
    CMD --> AC3
    GRID --> DC
    GRID --> AC1
    GRID --> AC2
    GRID --> AC3
    DC -- TopologyPushResult, Started, Stopped --> RES
    RES --> AC1
    RES --> AC2
    RES --> AC3
    AC1 -- AC pushes and rejections --> RES
    AC2 --> RES
    AC3 --> RES
    DC --> HB
    AC1 --> HB
    AC1 --> LF
    AC2 --> LF
    AC3 --> LF

State by location: in Kafka, every command and every result (commands, results shared by both stages, heartbeat, plus the three importer topics), durable and replayable from any offset; on the shared file system, the processed grid folder written by the importer and preprocessing (Lab step 1) and the AC load-flow results (loadflow_result_fs, the StoredLoadflowReference of each AC topology); only in a worker's memory, the DC repertoire (device arrays) and each AC worker's ac_optim_topology and finished_optimizations tables, its parent_id lineage and acceptance flags. Three AC workers each build their own copy of the table from the results topic, so the picture has three private databases that never agree exactly (each has consumed up to its own offset and each ran its own mutations). A restart of AC worker 2 loses its table, the AC candidates it was evaluating and its knowledge of which optimizations finished; it recovers the DC candidates only if its consumer group re-reads results from the beginning. To restart without losing work: (1) move the store out of the process, either create_engine('sqlite:///<file on the shared file system>') or a PostgreSQL service, so ACOptimTopology survives and can be shared by the three workers, and keep scrub_db as the retention policy; (2) commit Kafka offsets only after the row is in that database, so a crash between consume and insert replays the message and the unique strategy_hash makes the replay idempotent; (3) publish the AC results, the accepted topologies and finished_optimizations as messages (they already go to results) so that a fresh worker rebuilds the lineage from the log; (4) make the AC worker's own loop restartable by writing a periodic checkpoint of the optimization it is working on (optimization_id, offsets, current candidates) next to the load-flow results. With (1) and (2) the SQLite memory box disappears from the diagram and the only non-durable state left is the DC repertoire, which the DC worker already rebuilds from OptimizationStartedResult plus the pushes it re-sends.

docs.title: Chapter 35. Capstone: reading ToOp end to end
docs.text:
Weeks: 5 · Semester: 5 · Prerequisites: Chapter 18, Chapter 22, Chapter 28, Chapter 29, Chapter 33, Chapter 34

Why it matters for ToOp

The capstone is where comprehension becomes contribution. Teams read ToOp end to end (papers, notebooks, code), test what its documentation claims against what its code does, and complete one project that answers a research question or improves the engine. Every team also writes the document an operator would actually read before switching: a short brief with the proposed topologies, their AC validation, the switching steps and before/after single-line diagrams. The skills transfer to any topology optimization software: read the paper, run the pipeline, distrust the docs, measure, and explain the result to the person who has to act on it.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
• Reading a research code base in layers: papers → runnable notebooks → a traced call path through the code.
  • Critical reading: documentation, docstrings and parameters that disagree with the code; turning each discrepancy into an issue, a test or a pull request.
  • A research question, a reproducible experiment (Chapter 26) and an honest comparison against a baseline.
  • Contributing upstream: fork, branch, Conventional Commits pull request title, DCO sign-off, pre-commit hooks and CI (docs/contribution_guide.md, .github/workflows/validate_pr_title.yaml, .github/workflows/ci.yaml).
  • Communicating with operators: from index lists (actions, disconnections, pst_setpoints) to switch operations (orao_summary.json), AC metrics (ac_metrics.json vs unsplit_ac_metrics.json) and single-line diagrams.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Trace one candidate topology from the genetic operators through the DC solver, the repertoire and the AC validation, naming the function and data structure at every step.
  • Verify or refute a claim in ToOp's documentation against the code, and back the verdict with a test or a minimal reproduction.
  • Design, run and report a reproducible experiment that answers a stated research question.
  • Write a 1–2 page operator brief that a control-room engineer could act on.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• Papers: "Accelerated DC loadflow solver for topology optimization", arXiv:2501.17529 (solver); "Bus Split Distribution Factors", TechRxiv, doi:10.36227/techrxiv.22298950.v1 (BSDF); arXiv:2412.16164 (unified derivation of distribution factors); arXiv:1606.07276 (MODF); "Transmission Topology Optimization using accelerated MapElites", arXiv:2605.10128 (optimizer).
  • ToOp documentation: https://eliagroup.github.io/ToOp/; docs/architecture/; docs/topology_optimizer/metrics.md; docs/topology_optimizer/ac/select_strategy.md and docs/topology_optimizer/ac/early_stopping.md; docs/contribution_guide.md; docs/wall_of_shame.md (known shortcuts and unfixed bugs). Coding conventions: .github/copilot-instructions.md.
  • Contributing: GitHub, "Fork a repository" https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/fork-a-repo and "Creating a pull request from a fork" https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request-from-a-fork; Conventional Commits 1.0.0 https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/; commitizen https://commitizen-tools.github.io/commitizen/; pre-commit https://pre-commit.com/; Developer Certificate of Origin https://developercertificate.org/.
  • Single-line diagrams: pypowsybl, "Network visualization" https://powsybl.readthedocs.io/projects/pypowsybl/en/stable/user_guide/network_visualization.html; ToOp's grid_helpers/powsybl/single_line_diagram/get_single_line_diagram_custom.py.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. Papers: arXiv:2501.17529 (solver), the BSDF paper, arXiv:2412.16164, arXiv:1606.07276 (MODF), then arXiv:2605.10128 (optimizer).
  2. Notebooks:
    • notebooks/example1_dc_loadflow_example.ipynb → notebooks/example_asset_topology_analysis.ipynb.
    • AC N-1 contingency analysis: build the Nminus1Definition yourself and call get_ac_loadflow_results, as in the lab of Chapter 19 (packages/contingency_analysis_pkg/README.md), not notebooks/run_ac_contingency_analysis.ipynb, which does not run (see the discrepancy list).
    • notebooks/example2_small_grid_toop.ipynb, remembering that its busbar-outage keywords are ignored → notebooks/example3_e2e_pipeline.ipynb.
    • Optional: notebooks/openrao.ipynb (Chapter 21); like the AC contingency notebook, it is not executed by CI.
  3. Code: trace one topology from optimizer/dc/genetic_functions/ through dc_solver/jax/compute_batch.py (compute_bsdf_lodf_static_flows) and dc_solver/jax/aggregate_results.py back to the repertoire, then to optimizer/ac/select_strategy.py and optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py.

docs.title: Documentation vs code: known discrepancies
docs.text:
Useful for critical reading exercises and for the documentation audit project (see also Appendix C). Each item was checked against ToOp commit ba1874e; re-check before you rely on it, since the code moves.

Documentation and docstrings

  • The README's "Pareto front" is a weighted-sum MAP-Elites repertoire (Chapter 27).
  • "(G)LODF" in the docs corresponds to LODF (single outage) and MODF (multi-outage) in the code.
  • The MODF citation differs between the dc_solver README (arXiv:1606.07276) and dc_solver/jax/multi_outages.py (doi:10.1109/TPWRS.2009.2023273).
  • docs/dc_solver/switching_distance.md describes a graph edge-cut algorithm; the code enumerates all coupler states (up to 20 couplers) and keeps those giving exactly two components (dc_solver/preprocess/preprocess_switching.py). The same page says a multi-connected asset keeps the busbar with the most other branches, while fix_multi_connected_without_coupler (grid_helpers/asset_topology_helpers.py) removes the connection to the lower-index busbar.
  • The package documentation lists three AC evolution operators; optimizer/ac/evolution_functions.py implements only pull.
  • docs/usage.md shows worker launch commands (python3 worker.py --processed_gridfile_folder=...) that the worker modules do not implement: optimizer/dc/worker/worker.py and optimizer/ac/worker.py have no CLI, and their main() expects ready-made Kafka producers, consumers and file systems (see their signatures, and "What is not included" in the course fork's docker/README.md).
  • docs/dc_solver/quickstart.md calls run_solver(topology, None, injection, static_information); the current signature takes (topologies, disconnections, injections, dynamic_information, solver_config).
  • docs/topology_optimizer/metrics.md itself states that the AC stage counts switching_distance differently from the DC stage ("This is a bug, not a feature"), so DC and AC switching distances of the same topology are not comparable.
  • packages/dc_solver_pkg/README.md says to set static_information.solver_config.cross_coupler_flow = True, but SolverConfig (dc_solver/jax/types.py) has no such field (on a plain dataclass the assignment silently adds an unused attribute). The batch path always computes N-0 flows through compute_cross_coupler_flows from unsplit_flow (dc_solver/jax/compute_batch.py), and LoadflowSolverParameters.cross_coupler_flow (optimizer/interfaces/messages/dc_params.py) is not read anywhere else.
  • The PowsyblBackend class docstring assumes "no HVDC lines" and "no batteries", yet _get_injections gathers batteries and LCC/VSC converter stations (dc_solver/preprocess/powsybl/powsybl_backend.py).
  • The docstrings of compute_cross_coupler_flows and _gather_bus_a_injection (dc_solver/jax/cross_coupler_flow.py) say True means busbar A, but the code, consistently with get_bus_data (dc_solver/jax/bsdf.py) and get_injection_per_bus (dc_solver/jax/injections.py), treats False as busbar A and True as busbar B.
  • The perform_outage_single_busbar docstring (dc_solver/jax/busbar_outage.py) says load flows are set to zero when both attempts fail; the code sets them to NaN.
  • docs/benchmark.md points to toop-engine-benchmark/config/ and assess_benchmark.py (the real names are configs/ and assess_benchmarks.py) and sweeps ga_config.split_subs, which is not a field of BatchedMEParameters.
  • docs/topology_optimizer/metrics.md calls the "exponential" overload metric exponential although it is a power law, describes N-1 overload energy per timestep although the code takes the worst contingency per branch, and states that bb_outage_penalty is zero when the topology is not worse than the baseline, which only holds with clip_bb_outage_penalty enabled (default off) (Chapter 19).
  • docs/dc_solver/preprocessing.md lists the preprocessing stages in a different order from the code, says relevant stations need 4 branches (the code requires 4 non-bridge branches), describes a one-hop node reduction (the code keeps two hops), and lists asset-topology files that a real import does not write (Chapter 22).
  • The action-set clipping docstring mentions 2**20 actions; the default clip_to_n_actions is 2**23 (dc_solver/preprocess/action_set.py).
  • Parallel PST group docstrings say groups are identified "during importing"; they are built in the dc_solver PowSyBl helpers (dc_solver/preprocess/powsybl/powsybl_helpers.py).
  • The loadflow-based artificial limits are named loadflow_based_n0/loadflow_based_n1 in the code, not border_limit_* as the AreaSettings docstrings say, and the LimitAdjustmentParameters docstring states its comparison the wrong way round (importer/pypowsybl_import/loadflow_based_current_limits.py).
  • The PreprocessParameters docstrings omit the 90–100 % dead zone of double limits (dc_solver/jax/aggregate_results.py), and the changing_switches_to_orao_dict docstring shows PST and TERMINALS_CONNECTION entries in the OpenRAO summary; optimizer/ac/summary.py emits only SWITCH entries and never exports PST setpoints.
  • The relay example in docs/contingency_analysis/cascade.md (80° characteristic) builds a self-intersecting polygon, which shapely reports as invalid (Chapter 20).

Notebooks and parameters that are silently ignored

  • notebooks/run_ac_contingency_analysis.ipynb does not run: it passes GridElement where Nminus1Definition.monitored_elements requires MonitoredElement, and its pandapower cell lacks a comma (method="ac" n_processes=15). CI never notices, because notebooks/tests/test_notebooks.py only globs example*.ipynb.
  • notebooks/example2_small_grid_toop.ipynb and toop-engine-benchmark/benchmark_toop.py pass enable_bb_outage and bb_outage_as_nminus1 to PreprocessParameters, which has no such fields and silently drops them; the preprocessing switch is preprocess_bb_outages, and the other two belong to the optimizer's ga_config.
  • compute_metrics_single_timestep (optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py) passes the misspelled keyword worst_k_contingent_cases to Metrics, whose field is worst_k_contingency_cases; the value is silently dropped.
  • early_stopping_non_convergence_percentage_threshold (optimizer/interfaces/messages/ac_params.py) and CLIArgs.checkpoint_frequency (optimizer/dc/main.py) are defined but never read; res_<epoch>.json is written at every epoch.

Behavior worth an issue

  • The PowSyBl backend negates phase-shift angles with the comment "TODO find out where this minus comes from..." (get_shift_angles in dc_solver/preprocess/powsybl/powsybl_backend.py); the sign convention is undocumented (Chapter 17).
  • run_solver (dc_solver/jax/topology_looper.py) builds a DefaultAggregateOutputFn that stores max_mw_flow and branches_to_fail and hashes as hash(solver_config). With the same SolverConfig object, a new DynamicInformation with different branch limits reuses the compiled program and returns results based on the old limits (Chapter 32 lab).
  • update_n0_for_pst_taps (dc_solver/jax/pst.py) discards the incoming N-0 flows, which the batch path derives from unsplit_flow, and recomputes them as PTDF·P, so any offset carried by unsplit_flow is lost when PST taps are optimized.
  • The 1×1 case of solve_and_check_det (dc_solver/jax/unrolled_linalg.py) checks a != 0 exactly, while the other paths use tolerances (LODF 1e-11, BSDF 1e-5, determinant 1e-10); a bridge whose denominator is numerically tiny but not zero can pass.
  • plot_repertoire (optimizer/dc/repertoire/plotting.py) fills empty repertoire cells with 1.05 times the minimum fitness, so empty cells look like very bad topologies rather than missing ones.
  • choose_max_mw_flow (dc_solver/jax/aggregate_results.py) places critical_branch_count_limited_n_1 in the N-0 group, so critical_branch_count_limited_n_0 is evaluated against the unlimited rating.
  • The DC N-1 oracle test test_nminus1_results_one_timestep is skipped, so only N-0 DC flows are cross-checked against an independent load flow (Chapter 33).
  • The import converts low-impedance lines to breakers only for the hard-coded UCTE area "D8" (importer/pypowsybl_import/preprocessing.py).

docs.title: Projects (one per team)
docs.text:
Every project states one research question, goes beyond the labs of Chapter 27, and follows the experimental methodology of Chapter 26 (budgets, seeds, repeated runs, statistics).

  1. Clean-room solver. Question: can the published papers alone reproduce ToOp's sensitivity factors, and where are they underspecified? Re-implement PTDF, LODF, MODF and BSDF in NumPy from the papers only, cross-check against ToOp on IEEE 57 and a node-breaker grid, and add Hypothesis property tests (Chapter 33) that ToOp could adopt.
  2. Pareto-based candidate selection for the AC stage. Question: does selecting AC candidates by Pareto dominance (with knee points or an achievement function) instead of ToOp's dominator filter raise the number of AC-accepted topologies per AC-second? Implement the alternative selection next to optimizer/ac/select_strategy.py, and compare both on a realistic grid with repeated runs.
  3. Multi-objective quality-diversity inside ToOp. Question: does a multi-objective repertoire integrated with ToOp's discrete repertoire find operator-relevant trade-offs that scalar MAP-Elites misses? Go beyond the stand-alone MOME lab: integrate it with the DC worker, and compare with scalar MAP-Elites by MOQD score and AC acceptance rate. The research survey found no published MOME application to grid topology, so a good result is publishable.
  4. Exact vs heuristic at scale. Question: up to what grid size and action space does ToOp reach within 1% hypervolume of the exact bi-objective front at equal wall-clock budget? Extend the exact baseline from IEEE 14/30 line switching to IEEE 118 and a node-breaker model with busbar splitting; compare AUGMECON2, NSGA-II and ToOp itself with anytime curves and ECDFs.
  5. DC–AC gap study. Question: which DC modeling assumptions best predict AC rejection of DC-optimal topologies, and can a cheap correction reduce rejections? Measure how often DC-optimal topologies fail AC acceptance (the lab of Chapter 28 checks one run on the node-breaker example grid), relate failures to the DC assumptions of Chapter 16, and test one correction or screening step.
  6. Documentation audit with real pull requests. Question: which discrepancies are documentation errors and which are code defects, and how many can be guarded by an automated test? Verify each item above. For each confirmed item, open an issue, then a pull request from a fork: a branch off main, hooks installed on the host (pre-commit install), commits signed off (git commit -s), a pull request title that passes commitizen in .github/workflows/validate_pr_title.yaml (for example docs: fix run_solver signature in quickstart), a test where the item is a code defect, and green CI (.github/workflows/ci.yaml, 90% coverage). Remember that the sensitive-file hook blocks .json, .xiidm and .hdf5 fixtures unless whitelisted.
  7. HVDC setpoint actions (improve ToOp). Question: how much N-1 overload energy can HVDC setpoint changes remove on their own and combined with topology, and does the DC estimate hold in AC? HVDCRange exists in interfaces/stored_action_set.py but is "currently not implemented yet in the solver", and dc_solver/preprocess/network_data.py always writes hvdc_ranges=[]. Model a link as a pair of injections (Chapter 11) whose flow sensitivities are PTDF column differences, extract ranges from the PowSyBl converter stations, carry setpoints as traced data next to the PST taps (dc_solver/jax/pst.py, dc_solver/jax/nodal_inj_optim.py), add a mutation operator, and validate in AC with pypowsybl on a grid with HVDC links.

docs.title: Operator brief (required deliverable)
docs.text:
Every team, whatever its project, hands in a 1–2 page brief for one congested grid situation, written for a control-room engineer rather than for a programmer:

  • Situation: base-case and worst N-1 overloads before any action (from unsplit_ac_metrics.json and the AC load flow results), and the data date and grid model used.
  • Proposed topologies: at most three, chosen by a stated criterion (for example the best AC-accepted topology per number of split substations), each with the overload energy removed in AC, the remaining critical branches, non-converging contingencies and voltage-angle differences (ac_metrics.json).
  • Switching steps: the ordered switch operations per topology from orao_summary.json, named by station and switch, with a feasibility note per step (breaker vs disconnector, synchro-check and angle difference; Chapter 20).
  • Diagrams: before/after single-line diagrams of every split station, with the changed switches highlighted (get_single_line_diagram_custom with highlight_grid_model_ids).
  • Assumptions and risks: DC–AC differences, contingencies not studied, and what would change the recommendation.

docs.title: Assessment rubric
docs.text: Criterion (weight) Excellent Adequate Insufficient Correctness (25%) Results agree with an independent oracle; every discrepancy found is explained Results plausible and partly cross-checked Unchecked numbers or unexplained contradictions Validation (20%) DC findings confirmed in AC N-1; limits of validity stated AC validation of the main result only DC-only claims Reproducibility (20%, Chapter 26) Pinned environment, seeds, configs and scripts regenerate every figure; repeated runs with statistics Most results rerunnable; few repetitions Single runs; results cannot be regenerated Code quality and tests (15%, Chapter 33) Typed, documented code; reference, oracle or property tests; pre-commit and CI green Tests for the main path only No tests, or tests that cannot fail Communication (20%) Report and operator brief are concise, correct and actionable; diagrams readable Clear report; brief lacks steps or diagrams Hard to follow; no usable brief

docs.title: Lab
docs.text:
Lab: a traced, reproducible baseline and a first operator brief

Tools: the ToOp container; Jupyter + pandas + matplotlib; pypowsybl single-line diagrams; git.

  1. Baseline run. Run the staged pipeline of notebooks/example3_e2e_pipeline.ipynb (run_preprocessing once, then run_dc_optimization_stage and perform_ac_analysis) on the node-breaker example grid data/grid_node_breaker/grid.xiidm with a fixed seed and runtime, three times. Store the configuration, res.json and the AC outputs of each run in your team repository, and tabulate initial_fitness, max_fitness and AC acceptance per run.
  2. Trace. Pick the best DC topology and follow it by hand: its actions and disconnections indices in action_set.json, the BSDF and MODF updates in dc_solver/jax/compute_batch.py, the metric in dc_solver/jax/aggregate_results.py, its repertoire cell, the AC selection in optimizer/ac/select_strategy.py and its AC score in optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py. Recompute its DC fitness from res.json as the negated weighted sum of target_metrics.
  3. Independent AC check. Rebuild the AC N-1 result of that topology, either with get_ac_loadflow_results on topology_N/modified_network.xiidm and an Nminus1Definition built with MonitoredElement (as in the Chapter 19 lab), or with create_loadflow_runner(data_folder, grid_file_path).run_ac_loadflow(actions, disconnections) (optimizer/benchmark/benchmark_utils.py), and compare with ac_metrics.json.
  4. Draft brief. Produce before/after single-line diagrams of the split station and a first operator brief following the template above; exchange briefs between teams for review.
  5. Pick your discrepancy. Verify one item of the discrepancy list with a minimal reproduction and file it as the first issue of your project.

Solutions: Lab · Notebook: lab_toop.ipynb (needs ToOp).

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
All statements are also in exercises.ipynb; the worked examples run in examples.ipynb.

  1. (Jupyter: pandas) From a res.json, rebuild the table of best_topos with fitness and every extra_scores metric, and check that fitness equals the negated weighted sum of target_metrics for every row. Which topology would you give an operator who accepts at most one split substation?

    Solution: Exercise 1.

  2. (ToOp container) Reproduce the silent drop of worst_k_contingent_cases in optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py with a two-line example, write the failing test, and draft the pull request title and body as they would pass validate_pr_title.yaml.

    Solution: Exercise 2.

  3. (Jupyter: pypowsybl) For one split station, generate the before and after single-line diagrams, highlight the switches listed in orao_summary.json, and write the switching steps in operator language.

    Solution: Exercise 3.

  4. (Jupyter: NumPy + matplotlib) For the topologies of your baseline run, plot DC switching distance against AC switching distance. Relate what you see to the note in docs/topology_optimizer/metrics.md.

    Solution: Exercise 4.

  5. For project 7, derive the DC sensitivity of every branch flow to a setpoint change \(\Delta P\) on an HVDC link between buses \(i\) and \(j\), and show that it equals \(\Delta P\,(\mathrm{PTDF}_{\cdot,i}-\mathrm{PTDF}_{\cdot,j})\) up to the sign convention. Where would this column live in ToOp's data structures?

    Solution: Exercise 5.

  6. Pick one project and write a one-page experimental plan: research question, baseline, metrics, budget, number of seeds, statistical test, and the figure that would answer the question.

    Solution: Exercise 6.

docs.title: Chapter 35 – Solutions
docs.text:
Solutions of the Lab and the Exercises of Chapter 35 that have one; the projects and the operator brief are team work and have no single answer, but the Lab below is the baseline every team starts from. The code is in the chapter's src folder. Four programs read ToOp's output files and run anywhere: res_table.py, switching_distances.py, brief.py and hvdc_sensitivity.py. Three need ToOp's interpreter: baseline_toop.py (the staged pipeline, three runs), ac_check_toop.py and sld_toop.py; test_ac_check_toop.py holds the two-line reproduction of Exercise 2. The files under src/baseline/ (res.json, the two configurations, unsplit_ac_metrics.json, and ac_metrics.json plus orao_summary.json per validated topology) are what baseline_toop.py wrote with ToOp ba1874e in the course's ToOp container (image toop-course:cpu, docker run --cpus 4, the work folders in the named volume toop-course-runs): the node-breaker example grid three times with seed 1 and 10 s of runtime (python baseline_toop.py <work> <grid.xiidm> 3 10), and the complex example grid (data/complex_grid/grid.xiidm, an HVDC link; its preprocessing log reports 67 branches, 9 relevant substations and 121 actions) once with 25 s (... 1 25), because the node-breaker grid has one relevant substation and ten actions and cannot show more than two repertoire cells. An earlier run of the same script on the maintainer's Windows host, with the shims below, gave the same DC and AC figures; only the number of epochs differed. Every number below comes from these files or from the programs (python <name>.py; the _toop ones in the container).

Two Windows notes carried over from Chapter 34: the colons in ToOp's TensorBoard folder names (baseline_toop.windows_shim) and the zero time step between fast epochs (iterations_per_epoch=500); both are harmless in the container. Two more came up here: PreprocessParameters(preprocess_bb_outages=True) fails on a bus-breaker model such as data/case57_xiidm/grid.xiidm (convert_rel_bb_outage_data meets rel_bb_outage_zero_flow_br_indices = None), and the importer's default area settings leave that case57 file with no branches at all, so the capstone's richer grid is the complex example grid.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text:
1. Baseline run. baseline_toop.baseline(work_dir, runs=3, seed=1, runtime_seconds=10) copies grid.xiidm into the work folder, runs run_preprocessing once (PreprocessParameters(action_set_clip=2**10, preprocess_bb_outages=True), 8 s) and then, per run, run_dc_optimization_stage with BatchedMEParameters(random_seed=1, runtime_seconds=10, iterations_per_epoch=500, n_worst_contingencies=2, me_descriptors=(split_subs, 4 cells)), LoadflowSolverParameters(max_num_splits=3, batch_size=8) and perform_ac_analysis with k_best_topos=4; dc_config.json and ac_config.json are written next to the outputs, which is what goes into the team repository. baseline_toop.tabulate:

    Run initial_fitness max_fitness Iterations best_topos Validated Accepted run_0 −61.445 −42.345 39 1 1 0 run_1 −61.445 −42.345 55 1 1 0 run_2 −61.445 −42.345 55 1 1 0

    The three runs end with the same best topology (action 5, DC overload energy 42.345 MW against 61.445 MW unsplit) but with 39, 55 and 55 epochs: a fixed seed makes the random stream reproducible, a fixed wall-clock budget does not make the amount of work reproducible, which is why Chapter 26 asks for budgets in evaluations. The AC validation rejects the topology every time: evaluate_acceptance returns the criterion overload-energy with value_after = 25.377 MW, value_before = 16.336 MW (the unsplit grid in AC) and the threshold 0.95, so a topology that removes 19 MW of DC overload energy adds 9 MW of AC overload energy. Noted for the brief: the DC and AC figures of the same unsplit grid differ by a factor of almost four (61.4 against 16.3 MW), and 7 of the 18 AC contingencies come back without a result (status NO_CALCULATION, which ToOp counts as non-converging; step 3 shows which and why).

  2. Trace. Action 5 of action_set.json is the fifth local_actions entry: a split of the station VLevel2 (voltage level VL2) that moves line L12 to the second busbar, realized by opening the coupler VL2_BREAKER, opening the disconnector L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_0 and closing L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_2 (the orao_summary.json of topology 0; disconnections is empty). In the DC stage the genotype of a candidate is a vector of action indices per relevant substation (optimizer/dc/genetic_functions/genotype.py, mutated in mutation/); for a batch of candidates compute_symmetric_batch (dc_solver/jax/compute_batch.py) calls compute_bsdf_lodf_static_flows, which applies the BSDF update of the PTDF for each split (bsdf.py), the MODF update for the disconnections (multi_outages.py), then the LODF N-1 flows; aggregate_results.py turns the N-1 matrix into overload_energy_n_1 (42.345 MW), max_flow_n_1 (2.207), split_subs (1), switching_distance (2: the precomputed reassignment_distance of action 5) and top_k_overloads_n_1 (67.27 MW with n_worst_contingencies = 2). The repertoire (optimizer/dc/repertoire/discrete_me_repertoire.py) has one cell per value of the descriptor split_subs; the candidate lands in cell 1, beats whatever was there, and best_topos lists the best of every non-empty cell, here just this one, since the unsplit grid is the initial topology and not a repertoire member. The AC worker's select_strategy (optimizer/ac/select_strategy.py) filters the DC pushes stored in its database with the median, dominator and discriminator masks over the target metrics, and compute_metrics_single_timestep (optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py) scores the realized topology from the AC N-1 results (fitness = overload_energy_n_1 = 25.377). res_table.weighted_sum_check confirms the DC fitness: target_metrics = {overload_energy_n_1: 1.0}, so fitness = −1.0 × 42.3453 = −42.3453, and the check holds for every row of every baseline file.

  3. Independent AC check. ac_check_toop.compare rebuilds the AC result of topology 0 with create_loadflow_runner(data_folder, grid_xiidm).run_ac_loadflow([5], []) followed by compute_metrics_single_timestep: fitness 25.37695571260243 against 25.37695571260243 in ac_metrics.json, the largest gap over the 17 shared metrics being 0.0 (on the complex grid, \(9 \times 10^{-13}\)): this route is ToOp's own code path and agrees to the last bit, so it checks the files, not the method. independent_n0 loads topology_0/modified_network.xiidm with pypowsybl alone, runs an AC load flow and divides each line's current by its permanent limit from get_operational_limits(): 0.84607 on L3, against max_flow_n_0 = 0.84607 in the file; for the unsplit grid 0.8652 on L1 against 0.8652. On the complex grid the same lines-only figure is 0.979 (unsplit) and 1.704 (topology 0) against 1.241 and 1.945 in the files, because there the worst monitored element is a transformer, which the lines-only check leaves out: an independent check is only as good as its coverage of the monitored set. The lab's other route, ac_check_toop.n1_route, runs get_ac_loadflow_results outside the runner on topology_N/modified_network.xiidm with the preprocessed nminus1_definition.json (its monitored elements are MonitoredElement objects: 8 on the node-breaker grid, with 19 contingencies including the base case; 95 and 128 on the complex grid) and sums the overload energy again in pandas. With pypowsybl's default load-flow parameters it does not reproduce the files: the unsplit node-breaker grid gives 112.25 MW, 3 critical branches and no failed contingency, against 16.34 MW, 2 and 7 in unsplit_ac_metrics.json. With the parameters the preprocessing stored (loadflow_parameters.json, which create_loadflow_runner loads; ac_check_toop.stored_lf_params) it matches every validated topology on both grids: 25.37695571260243 MW for node-breaker topology 0, 1669.53 MW, 29 critical branches and 5 failed contingencies for complex topology 0, and the unsplit figures exactly. The 7 failures of the node-breaker grid are the three injection outages (generator3, load1, load2) and four of the seven busbar outages, all with status NO_CALCULATION: they are not divergences, they are cases the load flow refused to compute under the stored parameters, and with the default ones the same contingencies converge and add 96 MW of overload energy. On the complex grid the default parameters give 4 MAX_ITERATION_REACHED cases (one more line, L1) and 2166.60 MW against 2160.39 MW. An independent check therefore has to fix the load-flow parameters as well as the N-1 definition, and the brief should say that 7 of 18 contingencies were not computed, rather than "did not converge".

  4. Draft brief. sld_toop.diagrams(grid.xiidm, topology_0/modified_network.xiidm, orao_summary) finds the voltage level of the three switches (VL2), runs an AC load flow on both networks and renders both with get_single_line_diagram_custom(..., highlight_grid_model_ids=[the three switch ids]): two SVG files of 45,735 and 46,475 characters with 3 highlighted elements each, one per switch (ToOp adds the class highlight to the matching elements; the colour #0050fcff itself occurs 7 times in every diagram because it sits in the CSS, once per voltage class, so counting the colour says nothing), and the switch states read from both networks, VL2_BREAKER closed → open, L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_0 closed → open, L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_2 open → closed. brief.brief(run_dir) writes the draft: situation (unsplit AC N-1: worst N-0 loading 0.865, worst N-1 loading 1.235, overload energy 16.34 MW, 2 critical branches, 7 non-converging contingencies), one proposal (topology 0, one split, AC overload energy 25.38 MW, 1 critical branch, 7 non-converging contingencies, largest angle difference 1.8°, ratio 1.55 to the unsplit grid: not recommended), the switching steps in operator language with a feasibility note each (open the breaker VL2_BREAKER, a breaker can interrupt load current; open the disconnector L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_0 and close L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_2, disconnectors carry no load current, so the breaker in series must already be open), and the assumptions (the N-1 definition, the unexplained non-convergences, the diagrams). The honest brief for this grid says: no topology to propose, redispatch or accept the overload; the reviewing team should ask why 7 of the 18 AC contingencies are not computed (step 3) before anything else.

  5. Pick your discrepancy. Two reproductions are in the folder. (a) The silent drop of worst_k_contingent_cases: Metrics(fitness=0.0, extra_scores={}, worst_k_contingent_cases=['L8']).worst_k_contingency_cases is None (two lines), and the test test_ac_metrics_carry_the_worst_contingencies in test_ac_check_toop.py, which rebuilds the AC metrics of topology 0 and asserts that worst_k_contingency_cases is not None, fails on ba1874e (it is marked xfail(strict=True) so that the course's suite stays green and flips when ToOp fixes it): every ac_metrics.json of the baseline indeed has "worst_k_contingency_cases": null. (b) Not on the chapter's list: the tracked preprocessed folder data/grid_node_breaker/grid of ba1874e was written by an older ToOp and its action_set.json carries starting_topology and simplified_starting_topology instead of starting_bus_groups and simplified_starting_bus_groups; ActionSet forbids extras, so create_loadflow_runner raises a ValidationError with four errors and the AC stage of perform_ac_analysis cannot run on the tracked folder, which is why baseline_toop preprocesses the grid again rather than reusing it (Chapter 33, Exercise 3 shows the other side of extra='forbid': it is the strict model that caught the stale fixture).

docs.title: Exercise 1
docs.text:
res_table.best_topos_table flattens best_topos into one row per repertoire cell with actions, disconnections, fitness and every extra_scores key, and weighted_sum_check recomputes \(\mathrm{fitness} = -\sum_m w_m\, \mathrm{extra\_scores}_m\) over args.ga_config.target_metrics. Node-breaker grid, every run: one row, actions [5], fitness −42.345326, max_flow_n_1 2.207, overload_energy_n_1 42.345, split_subs 1, switching_distance 2, top_k_overloads_n_1 67.271; recomputed −42.345326, match. Complex grid (target_metrics = {overload_energy_n_1: 1.0}, initial fitness −1310.860, four cells):

Actions Fitness max_flow_n_1 overload_energy_n_1 split_subs switching_distance top_k_overloads_n_1 [1, 54, 68] −1160.366 2.663 1160.366 3 8 1104.256 [54, 68] −1169.118 2.728 1169.118 2 4 665.022 [69] −1184.119 2.663 1184.119 1 4 721.598 [] −1243.819 2.663 1243.819 0 0 698.462

fitness equals the negated weighted sum in every row of every file (matches is True throughout; with one target metric of weight 1 the check is \(\mathrm{fitness} = -\mathrm{overload\_energy\_n\_1}\), which is also why max_fitness in res.json is the first row). The operator who accepts at most one split substation gets the best row with split_subs ≤ 1, for_operator(table, 1): action [69], fitness −1184.119, which removes 60 MW of DC overload energy (5 %) against 83 MW for three splits, with the same max_flow_n_1; on the node-breaker grid the only candidate, [5], qualifies. And the pick comes with its AC verdict from the baseline: [69] is rejected (overload-energy, 2154.997 against 0.95 × 2160.388 MW), as are the other three (two of them by convergence, 5 non-converging contingencies against 3 unsplit), so the honest recommendation is none of them.

res_table.py
"""Read a ToOp ``res.json``: the ``best_topos`` table, the fitness check and the operator's pick (Chapter 35, Ex. 1).

The files under ``baseline/`` were written by ``baseline_toop.py`` with ToOp ``ba1874e`` (node-breaker grid, three
runs with the same seed; the complex example grid, one run); ``python res_table.py [res.json]`` prints the tables.
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

BASELINE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'baseline'
NODE_BREAKER = BASELINE / 'node_breaker' / 'run_0' / 'res.json'
COMPLEX = BASELINE / 'complex_grid' / 'run_0' / 'res.json'


def load_res(path):
    """The parsed ``res.json``."""
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))


def best_topos_table(res):
    """One row per entry of ``best_topos``: actions, disconnections, fitness and every ``extra_scores`` metric."""
    rows = []
    for topo in res['best_topos']:
        row = {
            'actions': topo['actions'],
            'disconnections': topo['disconnections'],
            'fitness': topo['metrics']['fitness'],
            **topo['metrics']['extra_scores'],
            'worst_k_contingency_cases': topo['metrics'].get('worst_k_contingency_cases'),
        }
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def target_metrics(res):
    """``{metric: weight}`` of the run, from ``args.ga_config.target_metrics``."""
    return {metric: float(weight) for metric, weight in res['args']['ga_config']['target_metrics']}


def weighted_sum_check(res, atol=1e-9):
    """Recompute ``fitness`` as minus the weighted sum of the target metrics and compare it row by row."""
    table = best_topos_table(res)
    weights = target_metrics(res)
    table['recomputed'] = [-sum(w * row[m] for m, w in weights.items()) for _, row in table.iterrows()]
    table['matches'] = (table['fitness'] - table['recomputed']).abs() < atol
    return table


def for_operator(table, max_splits=1):
    """The best (largest fitness) topology with at most ``max_splits`` split substations, or None."""
    eligible = table[table['split_subs'] <= max_splits]
    return None if eligible.empty else eligible.sort_values('fitness', ascending=False).iloc[0]


def main():
    """Print the table, the check and the operator's pick for the file given (default: both baselines)."""
    paths = [Path(sys.argv[1])] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else [NODE_BREAKER, COMPLEX]
    pd.set_option('display.width', 200)
    for path in paths:
        res = load_res(path)
        table = weighted_sum_check(res)
        print(
            f'{path.parent.parent.name}/{path.parent.name}: target metrics {target_metrics(res)}, '
            f'initial fitness {res["initial_fitness"]:.3f}, {len(table)} best_topos'
        )
        print(table.drop(columns=['worst_k_contingency_cases']).to_string(index=False))
        print('fitness equals the negated weighted sum in every row:', bool(table['matches'].all()))
        pick = for_operator(table, 1)
        print(
            'at most one split substation ->',
            None if pick is None else f'actions {pick["actions"]}, fitness {pick["fitness"]:.3f}',
        )
        print()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Open the src/ folder on GitHub to see or download all the files of this chapter.

docs.title: Exercise 2
docs.text:
The two-line reproduction (test_metrics_keyword_is_silently_dropped_in_two_lines in test_ac_check_toop.py):

metrics = Metrics(fitness=0.0, extra_scores={}, worst_k_contingent_cases=['L8'])
assert metrics.worst_k_contingency_cases is None

Metrics (optimizer/interfaces/messages/results.py) keeps Pydantic's default extra='ignore', so the misspelled keyword that compute_metrics_single_timestep passes (optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py: metrics.pop("worst_k_contingent_cases", None) and Metrics(..., worst_k_contingent_cases=...)) is accepted and discarded, and every AC Metrics leaves the worker with worst_k_contingency_cases = None; downstream, get_early_stopping_contingency_ids sees an empty list and logs "No overload threshold or case ids found", so the AC early stopping never gets the DC worst cases. The failing test is the second one in the same file, written against ToOp's own API so that it can move into packages/topology_optimizer_pkg/tests/: run the AC load flow of a topology through create_loadflow_runner, call compute_metrics_single_timestep, assert worst_k_contingency_cases is not None. It fails on ba1874e (marked xfail(strict=True) here) and passes once the keyword is spelled worst_k_contingency_cases on both the pop and the constructor. Pull request, as .github/workflows/validate_pr_title.yaml (commitizen's conventional commits) accepts it:

Title: fix: pass worst_k_contingency_cases to Metrics in the AC scoring

Body: compute_metrics_single_timestep builds Metrics with the keyword worst_k_contingent_cases, which the model does not declare; Pydantic ignores it, so the AC metrics never carry the worst contingencies and the early-stopping subset falls back to the full N-1 list (get_early_stopping_contingency_ids logs a warning on every topology). This renames the keyword in the pop and in the constructor, adds test_ac_metrics_carry_worst_contingencies (fails before, passes after), and sets extra="forbid" on Metrics so that the next misspelling is a ValidationError. Fixes #. Signed-off-by: .

The commit is signed off (git commit -s, the DCO check), the branch comes from a fork, and the hooks run on the host (pre-commit install); the extra="forbid" line is the part a reviewer may push back on, because other producers of Metrics may rely on the leniency, which is exactly the discussion the pull request should start.

docs.title: Exercise 3
docs.text:
sld_toop.diagrams and brief.switching_steps on topology 0 of the node-breaker baseline (the station VL2): the before and after diagrams are rendered from grid.xiidm and topology_0/modified_network.xiidm after an AC load flow, with highlight_grid_model_ids set to the three switch ids of orao_summary.json, which the custom style paints in #0050fcff (3 highlighted elements in each SVG, one per switch, counted by their highlight class). Read side by side, the before diagram shows the two busbars of VL2 coupled through the closed VL2_BREAKER, with line L12 on the first busbar (L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_0 closed, _4_2 open); the after diagram shows the coupler open and L12 on the second busbar. The switching steps in operator language:

  1. Open the busbar coupler breaker VL2_BREAKER (a breaker: it can interrupt load current; afterwards the two busbars of VL2 run separately, with the feeders as they are).
  2. Open the disconnector L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_0 to take line L12 off busbar 1 (a disconnector: it must not carry current, so L12 has to be de-energised or its breaker open at this moment; ToOp's switch list says nothing about the line breaker, which is the first thing the operator adds).
  3. Close the disconnector L12_DISCONNECTOR_4_2 to connect L12 to busbar 2 (again without current; then re-close the line breaker, and if L12 was kept live from the far end, synchro-check: the two ends are the same synchronous grid, the angle difference is the one across the open path, small here, 1.8° at most in N-1).

ToOp's ORAO summary gives the end state of the switches, not an operable sequence: the order above (coupler first, disconnectors with the feeder dead) is the operator's, and the orao_summary.json of ba1874e emits only SWITCH entries (no TERMINALS_CONNECTION, no PST setpoints), as the chapter's discrepancy list notes. For the complex grid the same program produces one pair of diagrams per split station (VL_2W_MV_HV_MV, VL_MV, VL_3W_HV for the three-split topology, 52 000 to 60 000 characters each).

sld_toop.py
"""Before/after single-line diagrams of a split station with the operated switches highlighted (Ch. 35, Lab 4, Ex. 3).

``diagrams(grid_xiidm, modified_xiidm, orao_summary)`` finds the voltage level of the switches named in the ORAO
summary and renders both networks with ``get_single_line_diagram_custom(..., highlight_grid_model_ids=...)``.
Run with ToOp's interpreter: ``python sld_toop.py <run folder> <data folder> [output folder]`` writes the two SVG
files and prints what they contain.
"""

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pypowsybl as pp
from toop_engine_grid_helpers.powsybl.single_line_diagram.get_single_line_diagram_custom import (
    get_single_line_diagram_custom,
)


def operated_switches(orao_summary):
    """``[(switch id, open?), ...]`` in the order of the summary."""
    actions = orao_summary['forced-actions']['preventive-actions-list']['actions']
    return [(a['switchId'], a['open']) for a in actions if a['type'] == 'SWITCH']


def stations_of(net, switch_ids):
    """The voltage levels that hold the switches, one per split station, in sorted order."""
    switches = net.get_switches()
    return sorted({switches.loc[s, 'voltage_level_id'] for s in switch_ids if s in switches.index})


def highlighted(svg):
    """How many SVG elements carry the ``highlight`` class that ToOp adds to the highlighted ids.

    The colour ``#0050fcff`` itself appears only in the diagram's CSS, once per voltage class, so counting it says
    nothing about which elements are highlighted.
    """
    return len(re.findall(r'class="[^"]*\bhighlight\b', svg))


def diagrams(grid_xiidm, modified_xiidm, orao_summary, style='bright_mode'):
    """``({level: (before svg, after svg)}, switch states before, switch states after)`` for the split stations."""
    ids = [s for s, _ in operated_switches(orao_summary)]
    before, after = pp.network.load(str(grid_xiidm)), pp.network.load(str(modified_xiidm))
    pp.loadflow.run_ac(before)
    pp.loadflow.run_ac(after)
    svgs = {}
    for level in stations_of(before, ids):
        svg_before = get_single_line_diagram_custom(before, level, custom_style=style, highlight_grid_model_ids=ids)
        svg_after = get_single_line_diagram_custom(after, level, custom_style=style, highlight_grid_model_ids=ids)
        svgs[level] = (svg_before._content, svg_after._content)
    states = lambda net: {s: bool(net.get_switches().loc[s, 'open']) for s in ids}  # noqa: E731
    return svgs, states(before), states(after)


def main():
    """Render the diagrams of every validated topology of a run and report sizes and switch states."""
    run_dir, data_folder = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
    out_dir = Path(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else run_dir / 'brief_sld'
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for path in sorted(run_dir.glob('topology_*/orao_summary.json')):
        summary = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        svgs, open_before, open_after = diagrams(
            data_folder / 'grid.xiidm', path.parent / 'modified_network.xiidm', summary
        )
        for level, (before, after) in svgs.items():
            (out_dir / f'{path.parent.name}_{level}_before.svg').write_text(before, encoding='utf-8')
            (out_dir / f'{path.parent.name}_{level}_after.svg').write_text(after, encoding='utf-8')
            print(
                f'{path.parent.name}: station {level}, {len(before)} and {len(after)} characters of SVG, '
                f'{highlighted(before)} and {highlighted(after)} highlighted elements'
            )
        for switch_id, _ in operated_switches(summary):
            print(f'  {switch_id}: open {open_before[switch_id]} -> {open_after[switch_id]}')
    print(f'written to {out_dir}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
brief.py
"""A first operator brief from the files a ToOp run leaves behind (Chapter 35, Lab step 4 and Exercise 3).

``situation`` reads ``unsplit_ac_metrics.json``, ``proposals`` the ``topology_*/ac_metrics.json`` files and
``switching_steps`` turns ``orao_summary.json`` into ordered operations in operator language, with a feasibility
note per step (breakers switch under load, disconnectors do not). ``python brief.py [run folder]`` prints the brief
of the node-breaker baseline.
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

BASELINE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'baseline'
NODE_BREAKER_RUN = BASELINE / 'node_breaker' / 'run_0'


def load(path):
    """A JSON file."""
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))


def situation(unsplit_ac_metrics):
    """Base case and worst N-1 figures of the grid before any action, from the unsplit AC metrics."""
    s = unsplit_ac_metrics['extra_scores']
    return {
        'worst N-0 loading': s['max_flow_n_0'],
        'worst N-1 loading': s['max_flow_n_1'],
        'N-1 overload energy (MW)': s['overload_energy_n_1'],
        'critical branches N-1': s['critical_branch_count_n_1'],
        'non-converging contingencies': s['non_converging_loadflows'],
        'DC fitness of the unsplit grid': unsplit_ac_metrics['dc_info']['fitness'],
    }


def proposals(run_dir):
    """One entry per validated topology with the figures the brief quotes."""
    out = []
    for path in sorted(Path(run_dir).glob('topology_*/ac_metrics.json')):
        ac = load(path)
        s = ac['extra_scores']
        out.append(
            {
                'topology': path.parent.name,
                'actions': ac['dc_info']['actions'],
                'disconnections': ac['dc_info']['disconnections'],
                'split substations': s['split_subs'],
                'DC overload energy removed (MW)': None,
                'AC N-1 overload energy (MW)': s['overload_energy_n_1'],
                'AC critical branches N-1': s['critical_branch_count_n_1'],
                'non-converging contingencies': s['non_converging_loadflows'],
                'largest voltage-angle difference N-1 (deg)': s['max_va_diff_n_1'],
                'critical voltage-angle differences': s['critical_va_diff_count_n_1'],
            }
        )
    return out


def switch_kind(switch_id):
    """Breaker or disconnector, read from ToOp's switch ids (``*_BREAKER*``, ``*_DISCONNECTOR_*``)."""
    upper = switch_id.upper()
    if 'BREAKER' in upper:
        return 'breaker'
    if 'DISCONNECTOR' in upper:
        return 'disconnector'
    return 'switch'


def switching_steps(orao_summary):
    """Ordered operations of an ORAO summary as sentences with a feasibility note each."""
    actions = orao_summary['forced-actions']['preventive-actions-list']['actions']
    steps = []
    for n, action in enumerate(actions, 1):
        if action['type'] != 'SWITCH':
            steps.append(f'{n}. {action["type"]} {action.get("id", "")}: not a switch operation, check by hand')
            continue
        verb = 'Open' if action['open'] else 'Close'
        kind = switch_kind(action['switchId'])
        if kind == 'disconnector':
            note = 'disconnector: no load current allowed, the breaker in series must be open first'
        elif verb == 'Close':
            note = 'breaker: closing joins two busbars, synchro-check and a small angle difference required'
        else:
            note = 'breaker: can interrupt load current'
        steps.append(f'{n}. {verb} {kind} {action["switchId"]} ({note})')
    return steps


def brief(run_dir=NODE_BREAKER_RUN):
    """The brief as Markdown text: situation, proposals, switching steps, assumptions."""
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    lines = ['# Operator brief (draft)', '', '## Situation (unsplit grid, AC N-1)']
    lines += [f'- {k}: {v}' for k, v in situation(load(run_dir / 'unsplit_ac_metrics.json')).items()]
    unsplit_energy = load(run_dir / 'unsplit_ac_metrics.json')['extra_scores']['overload_energy_n_1']
    for prop in proposals(run_dir):
        lines += [
            '',
            f'## Proposal {prop["topology"]}: actions {prop["actions"]}, disconnections {prop["disconnections"]}',
        ]
        prop['DC overload energy removed (MW)'] = None
        lines += [
            f'- {k}: {v}'
            for k, v in prop.items()
            if k not in ('topology', 'actions', 'disconnections') and v is not None
        ]
        ratio = prop['AC N-1 overload energy (MW)'] / unsplit_energy
        lines.append(f'- AC N-1 overload energy relative to the unsplit grid: {ratio:.2f}')
        lines += ['', '### Switching steps']
        lines += switching_steps(load(run_dir / prop['topology'] / 'orao_summary.json'))
    lines += [
        '',
        '## Assumptions and risks',
        "- DC optimization, AC validation with ToOp's N-1 definition; contingencies outside it are not studied.",
        '- Load flow convergence failures are counted, not explained.',
        '- Diagrams: before/after single-line diagrams of the split station with the switches above highlighted.',
    ]
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def main():
    """Print the brief of the run folder given (default: the node-breaker baseline, run 0)."""
    print(brief(Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else NODE_BREAKER_RUN))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: Exercise 4
docs.text:
switching_distances.all_pairs matches each topology_*/ac_metrics.json with its entry of res.json:

Grid Actions DC switching_distance AC switching_distance DC overload energy AC overload energy node-breaker (3 runs) [5] 2 3 42.3 25.4 complex [1, 54, 68] 8 12 1160.4 1669.5 complex [54, 68] 4 7 1169.1 1683.1 complex [69] 4 5 1184.1 2155.0 complex [] 0 (not reported) 1243.8 2160.4

The plot (switching_distances.plot, DC on the horizontal axis, AC on the vertical, one point per topology and the diagonal for reference) has every point above the diagonal: the AC value exceeds the DC value by 1 to 4 and the two are equal for none of the seven topologies, and the gap grows with the number of splits. The two numbers are not the same quantity. The DC stage (get_switching_distance in dc_solver/jax/aggregate_results.py) sums, over the applied branch actions, a reassignment_distance computed once during preprocessing, the number of branch reassignments of the action against the starting configuration; the AC stage (extract_switching_distance in optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py) counts the entries of the realized topology's branch_reassignment_diff plus injection_reassignment_diff after the action set has been applied to the real node-breaker model, where moving a line also moves what hangs on it and a coupler counts as an operation. That is the note of docs/topology_optimizer/metrics.md ("the AC solver counts this slightly differently than the DC solver. This is a bug, not a feature"): the same topology has two switching distances, the DC one is a repertoire descriptor (me_descriptors can bin on it) and the AC one is what the brief should quote, since it is closer to the operations of Exercise 3; and the unsplit topology has no AC value at all, because the AC metrics are only computed for k_best_topos candidates, the unsplit grid among them only by accident (the complex grid's cell 0).

switching_distances.py
"""DC against AC switching distance for the validated topologies of a baseline run (Chapter 35, Exercise 4).

The DC value is ``extra_scores.switching_distance`` of ``res.json`` (``get_switching_distance`` in
``dc_solver/jax/aggregate_results.py``: the precomputed ``reassignment_distance`` of each applied branch action,
summed). The AC value is ``extra_scores.switching_distance`` of ``ac_metrics.json`` (``extract_switching_distance``
in ``optimizer/ac/scoring_functions.py``: the number of branch and injection reassignments of the realized
topology). ``python switching_distances.py`` prints the pairs of both baselines and describes the plot.
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
import pandas as pd

matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

BASELINE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'baseline'


def pairs(run_dir):
    """One row per ``topology_*`` folder: actions, DC and AC switching distance, DC and AC overload energy."""
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    res = json.loads((run_dir / 'res.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    by_actions = {tuple(t['actions']): t['metrics']['extra_scores'] for t in res['best_topos']}
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(run_dir.glob('topology_*/ac_metrics.json')):
        ac = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        actions = tuple(ac['dc_info']['actions'])
        dc_scores = by_actions.get(actions, ac['dc_info']['metrics']['extra_scores'])
        rows.append(
            {
                'run': run_dir.name,
                'topology': path.parent.name,
                'actions': list(actions),
                'dc_switching_distance': dc_scores.get('switching_distance'),
                'ac_switching_distance': ac['extra_scores'].get('switching_distance'),
                'dc_overload_energy_n_1': dc_scores['overload_energy_n_1'],
                'ac_overload_energy_n_1': ac['extra_scores']['overload_energy_n_1'],
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def all_pairs(root=BASELINE):
    """The pairs of every run under ``baseline/<grid>/run_*``."""
    frames = [pairs(run_dir).assign(grid=run_dir.parent.name) for run_dir in sorted(root.glob('*/run_*'))]
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)


def plot(table, ax=None):
    """Scatter of AC against DC switching distance with the diagonal; returns the axes."""
    ax = ax or plt.figure(figsize=(4, 4)).add_subplot()
    for grid, part in table.groupby('grid'):
        ax.scatter(part['dc_switching_distance'], part['ac_switching_distance'], label=grid)
    top = max(table['dc_switching_distance'].max(), table['ac_switching_distance'].max(), 1)
    ax.plot([0, top], [0, top], 'k--', linewidth=0.8, label='equal')
    ax.set_xlabel('DC switching distance (reassignment_distance of the actions)')
    ax.set_ylabel('AC switching distance (reassignments of the realized topology)')
    ax.legend()
    return ax


def main():
    """Print the table and the facts the figure would show."""
    table = all_pairs(Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else BASELINE)
    pd.set_option('display.width', 200)
    print(table.to_string(index=False))
    diff = table['ac_switching_distance'] - table['dc_switching_distance']
    print(
        f'\n{len(table)} topologies; AC minus DC switching distance: min {diff.min()}, max {diff.max()}, '
        f'equal in {(diff == 0).sum()} of them'
    )
    plot(table)
    print('figure: one point per topology, DC on x, AC on y, with the diagonal for reference')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
